home.welcomeBody: MyArcheryDiary is your archery notebook, always at hand. Like a real notebook lying on your desk, it keeps track of every session: training, coaching, competitions and strength work. At the end of the season, generate your notebook as a PDF to print or share it.

audience.question: Who is MyArcheryDiary for?
audience.answer: Archers of every level who want to keep track of their practice, and their coaches: an archer invites their coach, who then follows their journal of the current season. At the end of the season, the archer can generate their notebook as a PDF to print or share it.

start.question: How do I get started?
start.answer: Create an account with your email or Google, then open your first journal. All that is left is to write down your sessions.

journal.question: What is a journal?
journal.answer: A period you name, usually a season. It gathers the events dated within that period in a calendar you can decorate and colour month by month.

events.question: What can I write down?
events.answer: Training, coaching, competitions and strength work, plus four types of your own. Each event has its sheet: scores, arrow count, self-assessment, feelings, photos, and the weather when shooting outdoors.

planning.question: Can I plan my sessions ahead?
planning.answer: Yes: for a day to come, note the duration, place, discipline, distance, goal and the session's outline, step by step. On the day, tick the steps done, then fill in the review. “Do this session again” creates a new one with the same programme, and your coach can suggest some too.

competitions.question: How do I find competitions?
competitions.answer: Choose your departments on the Profile page: the FFTA competitions of your disciplines show in your calendars, with the published invitations on the home page. The “Competition planning” window also shows them on a map, with the distance from your starting town; one click adds them to your journal, and their results open from the sheet once published.

progress.question: Where can I see my progress?
progress.answer: The Stats page shows your scores, your average per arrow at each distance, your arrow volume and your feelings, next to the goals you set yourself. The home page follows your regularity, and the “Season summary” sums up a whole season.

share.question: Can I share my season?
share.answer: Yes: each past session and your season summary can be posted on Instagram as a card, and “Journal publication” gathers calendars, indicators and sheets in a PDF to print or keep.

devices.question: On which devices?
devices.answer: Phone, tablet or computer, in your browser, in French or English. You can also add it to your phone's home screen and open it like an app.
